They tell me that the working world has lately been turned inside out by the practice of laboring at home, and that it is no passing fashion but a settled change in the manner in which a person lives and earns his bread. I have no means of checking this, and nobody I could find was willing to be named for it; but the thing does appear to be true, and I will take the word of the invisible gentlemen.

Employers have gone in heavily for the machinery of it, the screens and the chatting devices—the apparatus by which forty men who once shared a corridor may now share nothing but a grievance, at a distance. This they call collaboration.

The workers, for their part, may now choose the hours at which they labor, and the reports say that they get more done. I believe it. A man who is permitted to work when his mind is clear will accomplish more than one who must work when the clock says so.

Whether this will transform the workplace entire, as is prophesied, I cannot say. The prophets are always confident, and seldom at the scene.
